Both solutions give the same final answer, p^n + p − 1, and both use the same set of orders, p−1, p^{n−1}, and p^{n−1}(p−1). Their arithmetic is correct: (p−1) + p^{n−1} + p^{n−1}(p−1) = p^n + p − 1.

Both rest on the same unverified step: that the three subgroups are the cyclic subgroups of Aut(G) (which is cyclic of order p^{n−1}(p−1)) with those orders. I can't confirm from memory which three subgroups the Terwilliger-algebra classification actually lists. The orders could differ, for example if the trivial subgroup or a different divisor is included. So neither solution is independently verified, and the answer is equally uncertain for both.

Solution B is slightly better presented, since it names the subgroups and gives a clearer derivation. That is a presentation difference, not evidence of correctness.

WINNER: B
